body: It's good to have some documentation, but Godot is not following this convention. I don't know what should we do.

Changes to a third-party item involve keeping a patch to the original file so the dependency can be "reconstructed" upon upgrading it. For an example, see `thirdparty/spirv_reflect/patches` and the related info about it in `thirdparty/README.md`.

In the driver code we use an utility macro (not repeating the comment for every occurence):

```suggestion
	VkDescriptorSet *sets = ALLOCA_ARRAY(VkDescriptorSet, p_set_count);
```

For some reason, we're also using the thread-local vector approach in driver code, as stated here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99257/files#r1843284766

So, feel free to pick either. There will have to be a uniformity pass in the future.

```suggestion
void RenderingDevice::execute_chained_cmds(bool p_present_swap_chain, RDD::FenceID p_fence,
```

Feel free to read the `const` (I guess that ship already sailed), though.

There are cases where Godot follows doxygen documentation, such as:

- gdextension_interface.h
- `split_by_plane` in core/math/face3.h
- `hash_djb2` in core/templates/hashfuncs.h
- `jstring_to_string` in platform/android/string_android.h

I followed those same conventions.

I know it's rare and Godot doesn't have code comments (which is very bad) and there are no standards set; but the `r_immutableSamplers` parameter was simply important to clarify the gotchas (that caller promises not to bind a different sampler because that simply won't work).
Yeah, makes sense. Maybe this eventually becomes the standard to follow. In the meantime, there's no real reson to discuss it. I just stroke my eye.

Done.

Switched to thread_local.

```suggestion
			The number of descriptors per pool. The Vulkan rendering driver uses linear pools for descriptors that will be created and destroyed within a single frame. Instead of destroying every single descriptor every frame, they all can be destroyed at once by resetting the pool they belong to.
```
Try to avoid ambiguous "backend", prefer explicit "renderer/rendering method" or "rendering driver", see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98744.

+			The number of descriptors per pool. Godot's Vulkan backend uses linear pools for descriptors that will be created and destroyed within a single frame. Instead of destroying every single descriptor every frame, they all can be destroyed at once by resetting the pool they belong to.
+			A larger number is more efficient up to a limit, after that it will only waste RAM (maximum efficiency is achieved when there is no more than 1 pool per frame). A small number could end up with one pool per descriptor, which negatively impacts performance.

body:
Hi, it's not HW dependent. The value of 64 is arbitrary.

Ideally this should not be necessary, see my [main post](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99257#issue-2660367614) when I refer to it:

> **Possible improvement for later:** It should be possible for Godot to adapt to how many descriptors per pool are needed on a per-key basis (i.e. grow their capacity like `std::vector` does) after rendering a few frames; which would be better than the current solution of having a single global value for all pools (`max_descriptors_per_pool`) that the user needs to tweak.

I added `0003-VMA-add-vmaCalculateLazilyAllocatedBytes.patch`.

There was no need to modify `thirdparty/README.md` because VMA already has custom patches and has a section for it.

The only thing I noticed is that the already-existing patches (`VKEnumStringHelper-use-godot-vulkan.patch` and `VMA-use-godot-vulkan.patch`) do not say in which order have to be applied (maybe any order works).

Which is why I named `0003-VMA-add-vmaCalculateLazilyAllocatedBytes.patch` starting with `0003` to indicate it's the 3rd one that needs to be applied.

This convention is used by git if you ask git to generate the patches for you. You can see the only one following this convention is the collection of patches in `thirdparty/vhacd`.
